families.name: Arduino Nano Family
families.tagline: Compact 45×18 mm breadboard boards spanning 6 distinct architectures — NEVER assume Nano variants share voltage, MCU, or pin rules.
families.familyWarning: CRITICAL: Nano Classic and Nano Every operate at 5V logic, whereas Nano 33 IoT, Nano 33 BLE/Sense, Nano ESP32, and Nano RP2040 Connect operate at STRICT 3.3V logic ONLY. Feeding 5V into a 3.3V Nano pin can permanently destroy the chip.

families.name: Arduino Mega Family
families.tagline: Expanded 5V robotics workhorse with 54 digital pins, 16 analog inputs, 15 PWM channels, and 4 independent hardware UARTs.
families.familyWarning: Mega 2560 uses 5V logic like Uno R3, but its I2C (D20/D21) and SPI (D50–D53) pins sit on different pin numbers than Uno R3. Never pull heavy total current across all 54 pins simultaneously.

families.name: ESP32 Family

families.familyWarning: STRICT 3.3V LOGIC ONLY across every ESP32 variant. Furthermore, 'ESP32' is a family of distinct chips (Xtensa vs RISC-V, Wi-Fi+BT vs Wi-Fi-only vs Wi-Fi 6 + 802.15.4) placed onto different third-party DevKits with varying pinouts and USB bridges.
